title: Basis Functions for the Baseline Hazard
text: Cox proportional hazards model specifies hazard subject ii h(ti)=h0(ti)e𝒙𝜷,h(t_i) = h_0(t_i)\,e^{\mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta}}, 𝜷\boldsymbol{\beta} collects regression coefficients h0(⋅)h_0(\cdot) unspecified baseline hazard. Maximum penalised likelihood (MPL) estimation approximates h0h_0 finite mixture non-negative basis functions ψ1,…,ψm\psi_1, \ldots, \psi_m: h0(t)=∑u=1mθuψu(t),H0(t)=∫t(1)th0(v)dv=∑u=1mθuΨu(t),h_0(t) = \sum_{u=1}^{m} \theta_u\,\psi_u(t), \qquad H_0(t) = \int_{t_{(1)}}^{t} h_0(v)\,dv = \sum_{u=1}^{m} \theta_u\,\Psi_u(t), Ψu(t)=∫t(1)tψu(v)dv\Psi_u(t) = \int_{t_{(1)}}^{t}\psi_u(v)\,dv cumulative basis 𝜽=(θ1,…,θm)T≥𝟎\boldsymbol{\theta} = (\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_m)^T \geq \mathbf{0} coefficients estimated alongside 𝜷\boldsymbol{\beta}(Ma et al. 2014, 2024). survivalMPL provides four production basis types, selectable via basis argument coxph_mpl.control(): rest article presents mathematical definition basis, visualises shapes, compares fits bundled melanoma dataset.

title: Basis Functions for the Baseline Hazard
text: time range [t(1),t(n)][t_{(1)}, t_{(n)}] partitioned mm adjacent intervals [αu,αu+1)[\alpha_u, \alpha_{u+1}). density cumulative bases ψu(t)=𝟏(αu≤t<αu+1),\psi_u(t) = \mathbf{1}(\alpha_u \leq t < \alpha_{u+1}), Ψu(t)=𝟏(αu≤t)[t𝟏(t<αu+1)αu+1𝟏(αu+1≤t)−αu].\Psi_u(t) = \mathbf{1}(\alpha_u \leq t)   \Bigl[t^{\mathbf{1}(t < \alpha_{u+1})}\,\alpha_{u+1}^{\mathbf{1}(\alpha_{u+1} \leq t)}         - \alpha_u\Bigr]. θu\theta_u interpreted directly constant hazard rate [αu,αu+1)[\alpha_u, \alpha_{u+1}).

title: Basis Functions for the Baseline Hazard
text: Basis function uu truncated Gaussian density centred knot αu\alpha_u scale σu\sigma_u: ψu(t)=1σuδuϕ(t−αuσu),Ψu(t)=1δu[Φ(t−αuσu)−Φ(t(1)−αuσu)],\psi_u(t) = \frac{1}{\sigma_u\,\delta_u}\,   \phi\!\left(\frac{t - \alpha_u}{\sigma_u}\right), \qquad \Psi_u(t) = \frac{1}{\delta_u}   \left[\Phi\!\left(\frac{t - \alpha_u}{\sigma_u}\right)        -\Phi\!\left(\frac{t_{(1)} - \alpha_u}{\sigma_u}\right)\right], ϕ\phi Φ\Phi standard normal density CDF, δu=Φ(t(n)−αuσu)−Φ(t(1)−αuσu)\delta_u = \Phi\!\left(\tfrac{t_{(n)}-\alpha_u}{\sigma_u}\right)            -\Phi\!\left(\tfrac{t_{(1)}-\alpha_u}{\sigma_u}\right) ensures truncated basis integrates 1 [t(1),t(n)][t_{(1)}, t_{(n)}].

title: Basis Functions for the Baseline Hazard
text: M-splines order oo built recursively augmented knots 𝜶⋆=[α1𝟏o−1T,𝜶T,αnα𝟏o−1T]T\boldsymbol{\alpha}^\star = \bigl[\alpha_1 \mathbf{1}_{o-1}^T,\,\boldsymbol{\alpha}^T,\,\alpha_{n_\alpha}\mathbf{1}_{o-1}^T\bigr]^T: ψuo(t)={𝟏(αu⋆≤t<αu+1⋆)αu+1⋆−αu⋆o=1,oo−1𝟏(αu⋆≤t<αu+o⋆)αu+o⋆−αu⋆[(t−αu⋆)ψuo−1(t)+(αu+o⋆−t)ψu+1o−1(t)]otherwise.\psi^o_u(t) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\mathbf{1}(\alpha^\star_u \leq t < \alpha^\star_{u+1})}       {\alpha^\star_{u+1} - \alpha^\star_u} & o = 1,\\[8pt] \dfrac{o}{o-1} \dfrac{\mathbf{1}(\alpha^\star_u \leq t < \alpha^\star_{u+o})}       {\alpha^\star_{u+o} - \alpha^\star_u} \Bigl[(t-\alpha^\star_u)\,\psi^{o-1}_u(t)      +(\alpha^\star_{u+o}-t)\,\psi^{o-1}_{u+1}(t)\Bigr] & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} cumulative Ψuo(t)\Psi^o_u(t) -spline (integrated M-spline); ψuo\psi^o_u integrates 1 support [αu⋆,αu+o⋆][\alpha^\star_u, \alpha^\star_{u+o}]. survivalMPL defaults o=3o = 3 (cubic M-splines), second-order roughness penalty closed form.

title: Basis Functions for the Baseline Hazard
text: Epanechnikov basis functions compact parabolic support. interior functions (1<u<m1 < u < m): ψu(t)=6𝟏(αu⋆≤t<αu+o⋆)(t−αu⋆)(t−αu+o⋆)(αu⋆−αu+o⋆)3.\psi_u(t) = \frac{6\,\mathbf{1}(\alpha^\star_u \leq t < \alpha^\star_{u+o})   (t - \alpha^\star_u)(t - \alpha^\star_{u+o})}{(\alpha^\star_u - \alpha^\star_{u+o})^3}. endpoint functions (u=1u = 1 u=mu = m) use asymmetric variants ensure proper probability density support. Like M-splines, use augmented knot sequence 𝜶⋆\boldsymbol{\alpha}^\star.

title: Basis Functions for the Baseline Hazard
text: choice basis affects smoothness shape estimated baseline hazard rarely changes regression coefficient estimates substantially. fit interval-censored model four bases using bundled pseudo-melanoma data (time first local recurrence, n=300n = 300, true baseline h0(t)=t−1/2h_0(t) = t^{-1/2}).
code: data(melanoma) formula_mel <- Surv(t_L, t_R, type = "interval2") ~   Arm + Leg + Trunk + mm1to2 + mm2to4 + mm4plus + Female + Age_centred n_obs <- sum(melanoma$t_L == melanoma$t_R & is.finite(melanoma$t_R)) base_ctrl <- list(n.obs = n_obs,                   smooth = 0,                   max.iter = c(40, 2e4, 5e4)) fit_u <- coxph_mpl(formula_mel, data = melanoma,   control = do.call(coxph_mpl.control,     c(base_ctrl, list(basis = "uniform"))))  fit_g <- coxph_mpl(formula_mel, data = melanoma,   control = do.call(coxph_mpl.control,     c(base_ctrl, list(basis = "gaussian"))))  fit_m <- coxph_mpl(formula_mel, data = melanoma,   control = do.call(coxph_mpl.control,     c(base_ctrl, list(basis = "msplines"))))  fit_e <- coxph_mpl(formula_mel, data = melanoma,   control = do.call(coxph_mpl.control,     c(base_ctrl, list(basis = "epanechikov"))))

title: Basis Functions for the Baseline Hazard
text: four bases recover broad shape true Weibull baseline h0(t)=t−1/2h_0(t) = t^{-1/2} (dashed). smooth bases (Gaussian, M-Splines, Epanechnikov) produce continuous estimates; uniform basis introduces visible step artefacts diminish knots.

title: Basis Functions for the Baseline Hazard
text: "msplines" (default interval-censored data) - M-splines offer good balance smoothness computational efficiency. second-order roughness penalty exact closed form. "uniform" - fast simple; useful baseline comparison. Use knots (n.knots) hazard close piecewise-constant. "gaussian" - smooth, kernel-based; first- second-order roughness penalties available. Can slow many knots. "epanechnikov" - compact support like M-splines parabolic rather polynomial shape; second-order penalty supported.

title: Basis Functions for the Baseline Hazard
text: basis registry (R/basis.R) allows new basis types added without modifying existing code. file R/basis-bsplines.R includes skeleton showing implement three required functions (knots_fn, matrix_fn, penalty_fn) call register_basis(). See ?list_bases full list registered bases.

title: Comparing coxph and coxph_mpl
text: survival::coxph() maximises partial likelihood — function regression coefficients 𝜷\boldsymbol{\beta} , baseline hazard h0(t)h_0(t) profiled . survivalMPL::coxph_mpl() maximises penalised full likelihood, estimating 𝜷\boldsymbol{\beta} h0(t)h_0(t) jointly via smooth basis expansion. right-censored data non-informative censoring two approaches produce essentially 𝜷̂\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} standard errors (Ma et al. 2014), coxph_mpl additionally delivers smooth, closed-form ĥ0(t)\hat{h}_0(t) can plotted predicted without additional post-processing. tutorial uses lung dataset (survival package) — 228 patients advanced lung cancer, right-censored overall survival — compare: Regression coefficient estimates standard errors. 95 % confidence intervals (forest plot). Estimated baseline survival: Kaplan–Meier, Breslow (coxph), M-spline (coxph_mpl).

title: Comparing coxph and coxph_mpl
code: library(survivalMPL) #> Loading required package: survival #> Loading required package: MASS library(survival)  lung <- na.omit(lung[, c("time", "status", "age", "sex", "ph.karno", "wt.loss")]) f    <- Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex + ph.karno + wt.loss  # --- partial likelihood (coxph) --- fit_pl <- coxph(f, data = lung, x = TRUE)  # --- penalised full likelihood, M-splines (coxph_mpl) --- fit_mpl <- coxph_mpl(f, data = lung,   control = coxph_mpl.control(     basis    = "msplines",     n.obs    = sum(lung$status == 2),     max.iter = c(150, 7.5e4, 1e6)   ) )

title: Comparing coxph and coxph_mpl
text: estimates agree closely: full-likelihood approach recovers regression signal partial likelihood, near-identical standard errors. MPL SE reported uses sandwich variance estimator fixed smoothing parameter derived Ma et al. (2014) (equation 29), accessed via se = "M2HM2" package. Note age ph.karno shown per raw unit (10-year 1-point changes respectively) table; forest plot rescales per-10-unit changes visual comparability.
code: beta_pl  <- coef(fit_pl) se_pl    <- sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_pl)))  beta_mpl <- coef(fit_mpl) se_mpl   <- fit_mpl$se$Beta$M2HM2  tab <- data.frame(   `PL β`      = round(beta_pl,  4),   `PL SE`     = round(se_pl,    4),   `MPL β`     = round(beta_mpl, 4),   `MPL SE`    = round(se_mpl,   4),   `Δβ`        = round(beta_mpl - beta_pl, 4),   check.names = FALSE ) knitr::kable(tab, align = "rrrrr")

title: Comparing coxph and coxph_mpl
text: Three estimators baseline survival function S0(t)S_0(t), evaluated mean covariate values: Kaplan–Meier — nonparametric, unadjusted covariates. Breslow — Nelson–Aalen step-function baseline coxph, adjusted mean covariates via survfit(). M-splines (MPL) — smooth closed-form estimate coxph_mpl.  Breslow estimate step function jumps observed event times. M-spline estimate smooth construction closely tracks Breslow curve, avoiding staircase artefacts arise tied sparse event times.

title: Interval Censoring with survivalMPL
text: Survival times interval-censored event known occurred interval (tL,tR](t_L, t_R] rather exact time. common clinical studies patients examined periodically (e.g. follow-visits). survivalMPL handles partly interval-censored data — datasets may contain mix exact event times left-, right-, interval-censored observations. censoring type communicated survival::Surv(..., type = "interval2"). tutorial presents two examples Ma et al. (2024).

title: Interval Censoring with survivalMPL
text: compare MPL M-spline method partial likelihood (PL) midpoint imputation. true model Cox model Weibull baseline hazard h0(t)=3t2h_0(t) = 3t^2, covariates X1∼Unif(0,1)X_1 \sim \text{Unif}(0,1) X2∼Unif(0,5)X_2 \sim \text{Unif}(0,5), true coefficients β=[0.75,−0.50]T\beta = [0.75,\,-0.50]^T.

title: Interval Censoring with survivalMPL
code: library(survivalMPL) #> Loading required package: survival #> Loading required package: MASS library(survival)  # Write simulate() function to repeatedly generate a sample simulate <- function(n, pi_E, g1, g2){    # Simulate covariates   x1 <- runif(n, 0, 1)   x2 <- 5 * runif(n, 0, 1)   X <- cbind(x1, x2)   beta_true <- c(0.75, -0.5)   eXtB <- exp(X %*% beta_true)    # Simulate true event times   neg.log.u <- - log(runif(n, 0, 1))   y_i <- (neg.log.u/(eXtB))^(1/3)    # Simulate censoring types & times   u_E <- runif(n, 0, 1)   u_L <- runif(n, 0, 1)   u_R <- runif(n, u_L, 1)    t_L <- (y_i^as.numeric(u_E < pi_E)) *     (g1 * u_L)^as.numeric(pi_E < u_E & g1*u_L <= y_i & y_i <= g2*u_R) *     (g2 * u_R)^as.numeric(pi_E < u_E & g2*u_R < y_i) *     0^as.numeric(pi_E < u_E & y_i < g1*u_L)    t_R <- (y_i^as.numeric(u_E < pi_E)) *     (g1 * u_L)^as.numeric(pi_E < u_E & y_i < g1*u_L) *     (g2 * u_R)^as.numeric(pi_E < u_E & g1*u_L <= y_i & y_i <= g2*u_R) *     Inf^(pi_E < u_E & g2*u_R < y_i)    # Compute midpoint and censoring type for midpoint imputation   midpoint <- t_L + (t_R - t_L)/2   event <- rep(1, n)   event[which(is.infinite(midpoint))] <- 0   midpoint[which(is.infinite(midpoint))] <- t_L[which(is.infinite(midpoint))]    df = data.frame(t_L, t_R, x1, x2, midpoint, event)   return(df) }

title: Interval Censoring with survivalMPL
text: loop runs 100 replicates evaluated vignette build due computation time.
code: # Run a simulation study ch2_ex26_save = matrix(0, nrow = 100, ncol = 8) baseline_h0 = NULL  for(s in 1:100){    # Generate data set   dat <- simulate(n=500, pi_E = 0.5, g1 = 0.9, g2 = 1.3)    # Fit MPL model   fit.mpl <- coxph_mpl(Surv(t_L, t_R, type = "interval2") ~     x1 + x2, data = dat, basis = "m", n.knots = c(5,0))    # Save coefficient estimates & SE   ch2_ex26_save[s,1] <- fit.mpl$coef$Beta[1]   ch2_ex26_save[s,2] <- fit.mpl$coef$Beta[2]   ch2_ex26_save[s,3] <- fit.mpl$se$Beta$M2HM2[1]   ch2_ex26_save[s,4] <- fit.mpl$se$Beta$M2HM2[2]    # Fit PH model   fit.ph <- coxph(Surv(midpoint, event) ~ x1 + x2, data = dat)    # Save coefficient estimates & SE   ch2_ex26_save[s,5] <- fit.ph$coefficients[1]   ch2_ex26_save[s,6] <- fit.ph$coefficients[2]   ch2_ex26_save[s,7] <- sqrt(diag(fit.ph$var))[1]   ch2_ex26_save[s,8] <- sqrt(diag(fit.ph$var))[2] }

title: Interval Censoring with survivalMPL
text: fit MPL Cox model pseudo melanoma dataset: time first local recurrence n=300n = 300 patients. Recurrence times typically interval-censored, occurring patient visits doctor. Covariates: melanoma location first diagnosis (reference: Head & neck), Breslow thickness (reference: <1<1 mm), gender (reference: Male), centred age decades.

title: Interval Censoring with survivalMPL
code: simulate_mel <- function(n, pi_E, a1, a2) {   neglogU <- -log(runif(n))    location <- sample(c(1, 2, 3, 4), n, replace = TRUE,     prob = c(0.2, 0.15, 0.3, 0.35))   Arm   <- as.numeric(location == 2)   Leg   <- as.numeric(location == 3)   Trunk <- as.numeric(location == 4)    thickness <- sample(c(1, 2, 3, 4), n, replace = TRUE,     prob = c(0.15, 0.4, 0.3, 0.15))   mm1to2  <- as.numeric(thickness == 2)   mm2to4  <- as.numeric(thickness == 3)   mm4plus <- as.numeric(thickness == 4)    Female <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.4)    x8 <- rnorm(n, 56, 12)   x8 <- x8 - mean(x8)   Age_centred <- x8/10    X <- cbind(Arm, Leg, Trunk, mm1to2, mm2to4, mm4plus, Female, Age_centred)   beta_true = c(-0.56, 0.01, -0.22, 0.22, 0.87, 1.13, -0.17, 0.14)   eXtB = exp(X %*% beta_true)    y <- as.numeric((neglogU/(2 * eXtB))^(2))    # uniform variables   U_E <- runif(n)   U_L <- runif(n, 0, 1)   U_R <- runif(n, U_L, 1)    t_L <- y^((U_E < pi_E)) *     (a1 * U_L)^((pi_E <= U_E & a1 * U_L <= y & y <= a2 * U_R)) *     (a2 * U_R)^((pi_E <= U_E & a2 * U_R < y)) *     (0)^((pi_E <= U_E & y < a1 * U_L))    t_R <- y^((U_E < pi_E)) *     (a1 * U_L)^((pi_E <= U_E & y < a1 * U_L)) *     (a2 * U_R)^((pi_E <= U_E & a1 * U_L <= y & y <= a2 * U_R)) *     Inf^((pi_E <= U_E & a2 * U_R < y))    df = data.frame(t_L, t_R, X)   return(df) }

title: Ancillary Arguments for Controlling coxph_mpl Fits — coxph_mpl.control
text: n.obs Number fully observed (non-censored) outcomes. Required basis == "uniform" derive acceptable range n.events_basis. basis Basis used approximate baseline hazard. One "uniform", "gaussian", "msplines", "epanechikov". Defaults "uniform". smooth Smoothing parameter value. Defaults NULL (estimated via REML). Set 0 maximum-likelihood estimates. Must non-negative. max.iter Integer vector length 3 giving maximum iterations (1) smoothing parameter updates, (2) inner beta/theta updates, (3) total inner iterations. Defaults c(150, 7.5e4, 1e6). tol Convergence tolerance parameter change iterations. Defaults 1e-7. n.knots Integer vector length 2 controlling internal knots non-uniform bases. first entry sets quantile knots range.quant; second sets equally spaced knots outside range. Defaults c(8, 2) M-splines c(0, 20) otherwise. n.events_basis Integer giving number fully observed outcomes per uniform basis element. Must lie [1, floor(n.obs/2)]. Defaults round(3.5 * log(n.obs) - 7.5) valid. range.quant Length-2 numeric vector giving quantile range used setting quantile knots non-uniform bases. Defaults c(0.075, 0.9). cover.sigma.quant Proportion fully observed outcomes targeted within 0.025-0.975 interval truncated Gaussian bases tied quantile knots. Defaults 0.25. cover.sigma.fixed Proportion outcome range targeted within 0.025-0.975 interval untruncated Gaussian bases tied fixed knots. Defaults 0.25. min.theta Minimum baseline hazard parameter value reported; estimates treated zero (active constraints). Defaults 1e-10. penalty Integer specifying penalty order. First- second-order penalties available "uniform" "gaussian" bases; "epanechikov" uses second-order; "msplines" uses order - 1. Defaults 2. order Integer order "msplines" "epanechikov" bases (default 3). Order 1 M-splines correspond uniform bases; order 2 triangular bases. kappa Step-size reduction factor (>1) used penalised likelihood fails increase. Defaults 1 / 0.6. epsilon Length-2 numeric vector giving safeguards survival baseline hazard values avoid logarithm issues. Defaults c(1e-16, 1e-10). ties Strategy handling duplicated fully observed outcomes defining knot sequences. Use "epsilon" jitter duplicates small random noise; use "unique" drop duplicates. Defaults "epsilon". seed Optional seed (integer vector compatible .Random.seed) used ties == "epsilon"; preserves current RNG state set.

title: Fit Cox Proportional Hazards Regression Model Via MPL — coxph_mpl
text: coxph_mpl fits Cox proportional hazards model allowing right, left, interval censoring maximising penalised likelihood penalty term smooths baseline hazard estimate. Optimisation combines Newton step regression coefficients multiplicative step baseline hazard parameters enforcing non-negativity constraints (see Ma, Couturier, Heritier Marschner (2021)). covariate matrix centred optimisation; baseline estimates covariance matrices corrected afterwards using delta-method adjustment.
